title: India AI funding nearly doubles to $1.6B in Jan-Sept 2026: Tracxn
summary: Tracxn report shows India AI funding nearly doubled to $1.6B in Jan-Sept 2026
detailed: India AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, nearly double the level in the year-ago period, according to a report by Tracxn Technologies.

"India AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in nine months 2026, up 96% from $822 million in nine months 2025 and 162% from $616 million in nine months 2024, marking the highest funding total across the nine-month periods covered since 2019," the report by data intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies' said.
According to the 'India AI - 9M 2026' report, the funding was raised across 87 rounds, compared to 149 rounds during the year-ago period.
According to the report, 111 investors backed India AI companies in the first nine months of 2026, down from 169 in the year-ago period.
sentences: India AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in the first nine months of 2026, nearly double the level in the year-ago period, according to a report by Tracxn Technologies.
This, in fact, is the highest funding grosser across the nine-month periods covered since 2019.

"India AI companies raised $1.6 billion in equity funding in nine months 2026, up 96% from $822 million in nine months 2025 and 162% from $616 million in nine months 2024, marking the highest funding total across the nine-month periods covered since 2019," the report by data intelligence platform Tracxn Technologies' said.
According to the 'India AI - 9M 2026' report, the funding was raised across 87 rounds, compared to 149 rounds during the year-ago period.
This indicates that the increase was driven by a relatively small number of large deals.
Early-stage funding led the investment mix.
Mumbai overtook Bengaluru to become the city with the largest funding during the period.
The ten largest rounds in 2026 raised $1.5 billion, 90% of the $1.6 billion total.
Neysa, a Mumbai-based AI cloud provider, raised the largest chunk, a $600 million Series B in February, equivalent to 37% of all funding.
Sarvam, the Bengaluru-based generative AI developer, raised $255 million in a Series B in June and a further $90.4 million in August.
Yotta raised $150 million in July.
"Series A and later rounds fell 33% to 24 from 36, and first-time funded companies fell 60% to 24 from 60," the report said.
Globally, AI companies raised $383.5 billion in the first nine months of 2026; India's $1.6 billion was 0.4% of that, ninth among countries.
Early-stage funding rose 191% to $1.3 billion between January and September, up from $434 million in the year-ago period.
Early-stage rounds fell 38% to 21.
The average early-stage round was $60.2 million against $12.8 million in the year-ago period.
According to the report, 111 investors backed India AI companies in the first nine months of 2026, down from 169 in the year-ago period.
First-time investors fell to 43, and international investors fell to 29.
Peak XV Partners led early-stage investors with three investments, followed by Prosus and Khosla Ventures with two each.
Antler, IvyCap Ventures and Finvolve made two seed investments each, while SoftBank Vision Fund and Creaegis backed one late-stage round each.
